manual_task_hotspots.task: Taking order details by phone/email and keying customer name, address, billing and item data into order forms, then re-checking the order against prior information before release
Expediting and tracing shipments: conferring with warehouse, shipping and carrier staff to find delayed orders and updating customers on ship dates and delays
Handling 'where is my order'/complaint volume: answering calls and chats on order status, refunds, exchanges and billing adjustments, and checking that a promised fix was actually applied
Comparing disputed or returned merchandise against original requisitions and invoices, then preparing documents for returned goods
Three-way matching on inbound freight: examining shipment contents against manifests, invoices and orders, then recording weights, charges, damages and discrepancies
Preparing bills of lading, work orders and shipping documents, choosing shipping method/route/rate, and contacting carriers to arrange pickups
Physical cycle counting and stock record upkeep: counting received stock, recording it by hand or on computer, and reconciling inventory records to product movement
Front-of-shop admin: computing prices and totals, processing returns, placing special orders or calling other stores to locate items, and keeping sales records

automation_evidence.finding: Generative AI chat assistant for customer support raised issues resolved per hour by 14% on average across 5,179 agents (3M+ chats), with a 34% gain for novice/low-skilled agents and minimal effect on experienced agents; customer sentiment and employee retention also improved. This is the strongest causal evidence for the chat/support task that dominates e-commerce service work, though the site was a Fortune 500 software vendor, not a retailer.

Seven large randomized field experiments at a cross-border online retail platform (2023-2024, millions of users and products) found GenAI raised sales in most workflows, with effects from no detectable impact to 16.3% depending on how much the AI added over existing practice; incremental value was roughly $5 per consumer, gains came through conversion rather than larger carts, and return rates and product ratings did not worsen. Larger gains for less experienced shoppers.

Large field experiment with Alibaba's e-commerce after-sales chat operations: a GenAI assistant that drafted diagnoses and proposed solutions in the opening stage improved service speed and customer-rated (subjective) quality but had no significant effect on objective quality measured by customer retrials. Lower-performing agents gained most; top performers saw declines in both subjective and objective quality, consistent with workflow disruption.

Longitudinal field study in retail warehousing (2,086,260 storage-location visits, 57,239 in a human-robot hybrid setting) found follow-me cobot trucks cut picking time by as much as 33.57%; the benefit shrinks with heavier products, higher pick density and longer travel, so it is largest on short-distance orders.

Benchmark comparison of machine-learning demand-forecasting models on a US multi-channel retailer's store-level sales data: a hybrid random-forest + XGBoost + linear-regression model beat random forest, ANN, gradient boosting, AdaBoost and XGBoost alone (MAE 0.0024, R-squared 0.9551). Uses the public Kaggle/Walmart sales dataset, so it demonstrates method, not a live deployment's inventory or stockout savings.

In robotic fulfillment centers where automated guided vehicles bring shelf racks to pickers, pickers themselves become the throughput bottleneck - so automation shifts the constraint to human pick-rate rather than removing it. Relevant to sizing any 'lights-out warehouse' claim for a mid-size seller.

Census Business Trends and Outlook Survey: about 14% of Retail Trade businesses reported using AI in any business function as of May 3, 2026, versus 19.8% nationally; about 17% expected to use it within six months. Adoption baseline, not an outcome measure - it implies most independent retailers are still pre-deployment.

E-commerce platform admin, marketplace seller back-ends and EDI purchase-order feeds - INFERENCE: standard for online sellers and wholesale web shops, but not named in the O*NET data used here
constraints: PCI DSS applies to every entity that stores, processes or transmits cardholder data, including the merchant, its processors and service providers - so any agent touching payment fields, refunds or card data sits inside a cardholder-data environment with segmentation and assessor obligations.

New Jersey Data Privacy Law (P.L. 2023, c.266) took effect January 15, 2025: NJ consumers get access/correction/deletion and opt-out-of-targeted-advertising and sale rights, controllers must publish privacy notices and contract with processors. Customer-service and personalization agents handling NJ residents' order and browsing data fall under it.

Web accessibility under the ADA: DOJ guidance states businesses open to the public must make their websites accessible (WCAG-referenced), so AI-generated pages, chat widgets and product content create legal exposure, not just UX risk.

Landed-cost and customs classification workload: duty-free de minimis treatment for commercial shipments valued at or under $800 was suspended effective August 29, 2025, with per-item specific duties ($80-$200) allowed for postal shipments for six months - importers now need HTS classification and duty math per parcel.

NJ wage floor: statewide minimum wage rose to $15.92/hour effective January 1, 2026, compressing the savings from low-skill task automation and raising the bar for any labour-substitution business case.

Data minimisation by design: order records combine names, addresses, phone/email, purchase history and sometimes payment metadata. Agents should read from scoped, redacted tool calls rather than hold raw PII, and chat transcripts are discoverable records.
Seasonal peak concentration (Q4) means automation must survive 5-10x volume spikes; steady-state accuracy benchmarks understate peak failure modes.
trends: AI adoption in retail is running below the rest of the economy: ~14% of Retail Trade businesses vs 19.8% all-sector as of May 3, 2026, with ~17% expecting to adopt within six months (Census BTOS) - a large laggard pool for advisory work.

Employment in the clerical layer of order fulfilment is projected to shrink: BLS 2025-2035 projections show decline for Order Clerks (78,900 US jobs in 2025, 6,300 total openings over the decade, mostly replacement) and for Shipping, Receiving, and Inventory Clerks.

NJ trade/transportation/utilities employment was about 886,000 in September 2026 (preliminary), down 1.2% year-over-year, with NJ unemployment at 4.2% - a soft hiring market that reduces the labour-shortage urgency that usually drives automation spend.

Cost shock on the import side: the August 29, 2025 suspension of de minimis treatment moved hundreds of millions of low-value parcels into formal duty processing, pushing classification, duty calculation and landed-cost work onto small sellers and their 3PLs.

Wage floor ratchet: NJ minimum wage reached $15.92/hour on January 1, 2026, after scheduled increases since 2019, steadily raising the cost of the stocker/cashier/support roles that dominate retail headcount.

Margin pressure from returns and free shipping expectations shows up as service cost, which is where support-automation pilots cluster; note that the strongest e-commerce field evidence shows conversion gains, not return-rate improvements.
caveats: Wage figures are BLS OEWS May 2025 estimates as republished on O*NET's state wage pages; O*NET's headline wording says 'workers on average earn' while the underlying table column is the 50th-percentile (median) wage - the numbers here are the median column. No Middlesex County-specific OEWS cut was available, so the New York-Newark-Jersey City metropolitan area (which contains Middlesex County) is the closest local benchmark and NJ state figures are used as the primary. BLS's own New Jersey OEWS HTML page redirected to an index when fetched, so state and metro numbers were taken from O*NET's mirror of the same May 2025 BLS release rather than from bls.gov directly. Effect sizes come from large-platform settings (a Fortune 500 software support desk, a cross-border marketplace, Alibaba, one European retail warehouse); none is a New Jersey independent retailer, and none isolates a small-merchant cost structure, so transfer to a 5-50 employee NJ shop is an inference, not a measured result. Two studies are arXiv preprints (2510.12049, 2603.29888) and are rated Medium for that reason; the warehouse and forecasting studies are peer-reviewed but single-site or benchmark-dataset based. The tools list combines O*NET software-skill entries (explicitly sourced) with e-commerce platform and EDI categories that are general market knowledge and are labelled as inference. Vendor product claims and blog statistics were deliberately excluded rather than downgraded to Low. Several relevant paywalled studies (INFORMS Journal on Applied Analytics pop-up retailer forecasting; Journal of Operations Management cross-item learning intervention; AIS PACIS chatbot-vs-human comparison) could not be opened and are therefore not cited at all.
data_gaps: No Middlesex County or Edison-specific occupational wage or employment series was retrieved; the New York-Newark-Jersey City metro is used as a proxy.
No published study measures AI/automation outcomes specifically for New Jersey e-commerce or independent retail firms (time saved, error rates, cost per order).

No peer-reviewed evidence located on AI in returns/refund adjudication, invoice-to-PO reconciliation, or marketplace listing/catalog maintenance for small merchants - the tasks with the highest manual-hour density in this segment.
No reliable public figure for the e-commerce share of New Jersey retail sales, or for the number of NJ independent retailers with their own web shop.
O*NET task data is occupation-level and nationally normed; it does not tell us how much of a given retailer's week goes to each task.
BLS state OEWS HTML pages for New Jersey could not be opened directly (redirected to the tables index), so the underlying XLSX/state tables were not verified independently of the O*NET mirror.

Paywalled studies that would have strengthened the demand-forecasting evidence (INFORMS JAA 2022 pop-up retailer; Journal of Operations Management 2021 cross-item learning at an electronics distributor) were inaccessible and are excluded rather than cited from snippets.
No measurement of peak-season (Q4) degradation in AI agent accuracy or escalation rates was found.
